params.body:
**Triage proposal** (from the forwarded mail; change the labels if it is wrong)
Category: question  Priority: P3
Summary: A media prospect asked whether youth trends can be read per generation, per age segment and per industry. All three exist today; this issue records the answer for the pitch deck.

Source: Portal mail:62.

## The question

Can trends be shown per generation, per age segment and per industry?

## The answer: yes, on all three (read 19 November 2026)

**Per generation.** Gen Z (born 1995 to 2009), Gen Alpha (born 2010 to 2024) and ZAlpha (born 2006 to 2012, a lens over the border between the two). Millennials and Gen Beta are tagged as context only, as parents and children.

**Per age segment.** Gentells calls these lifestages, each with its age range: Kids (6 to 10), Tweens (9 to 10), Teens (11 to 17), Students (18 to 25), Young Adults (18 to 34) and Young Families (parents of 25 to 39).

**Per industry.** Twelve sectors: Fashion, Food & FMCG, Banking & Insurance, Employer Branding, Beauty, Media & Entertainment, Telecom & Tech, Automotive, Travel, Health & Wellness, Education, Government & NGO. Behind them sit seventeen topics.

Where a reader finds it:

- gentells.com/trends filters on sector (by topic, see below), generation and lifestage, and the three can be combined.
- The members' MCP server returns the same tags with every trend, so an assistant can answer per group and per sector.
- The Observatory compares generations and lifestages side by side.

Volume, from the Observatory's intake mix over the 90 days up to 19 November 2026 (kept signals; a signal can carry several tags): Gen Z 19,950, ZAlpha 1,674, Gen Alpha 713; Young Adults 18,783, Teens 13,920, Students 9,647, Tweens 3,648, Kids 1,521, Young Families 1,065.

## One thing to know before showing it

The sector filter on the trends page works on the seventeen topics, not on the twelve sectors: a choice there is a topic such as Music & Movies, Media & Platforms or Gaming. For a prospect in media and radio that is the useful cut: Music & Movies is the largest topic (10,683 kept signals in 90 days) and can be chosen directly.

The regional side of the same conversation (Flanders, Belgium) is a separate issue in gentells-standard.
params.title: Can trends be read per generation, per age segment and per industry? Yes, on all three
